reasons.label: My grades or a prerequisite
reasons.hint: Routes that don't depend on one tough course

reasons.label: I didn't get in
reasons.hint: Other ways in, like college and transfer

reasons.label: I don't enjoy this route
reasons.hint: Same goal, different kind of work

destinations.name: Software Developer
destinations.blurb: Design, build and maintain the apps and systems people use every day.

routes.label: Computer Science degree
routes.why: The classic route: programming, data structures and shipping a real app.

routes.label: Design first, then front-end
routes.why: Start from visual and UX design, then branch into coding what you design.

routes.label: Engineering, then software for machines
routes.why: Build hardware and code together, then specialize in the software side.

routes.label: College diploma + portfolio
routes.why: A two- or three-year programming diploma with co-op. You can work, or transfer credits to a degree later.

steps.title: Compare college programs
steps.objective: Compare two college computer programming diplomas: length, co-op and transfer options.
steps.learn: Colleges teach practical programming with smaller classes and co-op placements.

steps.title: Build three projects
steps.objective: Finish three small coding projects and put them on GitHub with a short README each.
steps.learn: A portfolio shows employers what you can do, whatever your grades.

steps.title: Plan a bridge to a degree
steps.objective: Look up which of your college credits would transfer to a university Computer Science degree.
steps.learn: Many colleges and universities have transfer agreements, so a diploma can lead to a degree.

steps.title: Land a co-op or junior role
steps.objective: Apply to three co-op, internship or junior developer roles.
steps.learn: Real experience is often the strongest part of a developer's application.

destinations.name: Cybersecurity Analyst
destinations.blurb: Protect networks and people's data by spotting and stopping attacks.

routes.label: Cybersecurity program
routes.why: Networking, Linux, cryptography and defending real systems.

routes.label: Computer Science, then branch into security
routes.why: Learn how software works first, then specialize in breaking and defending it.

routes.label: College diploma + certifications
routes.why: A cybersecurity or networking diploma plus industry certificates is a common, faster way in.

steps.title: Compare college programs
steps.objective: Compare two college cybersecurity or networking diplomas, including co-op.
steps.learn: Colleges offer hands-on security programs with lab time and placements.

steps.title: Build a home lab
steps.objective: Complete five beginner rooms on TryHackMe and write notes on what you learned.
steps.learn: Practising in safe, legal labs is how most analysts build skills.

steps.title: Earn an entry certificate
steps.objective: Study for an entry-level security certificate using free video courses.
steps.learn: Certificates show employers you know the fundamentals.

steps.title: Start in IT support
steps.objective: Apply to help-desk, IT support or security co-op roles.
steps.learn: Many analysts start in IT support and move into security.

destinations.name: Data Analyst
destinations.blurb: Turn data into answers that help teams make better decisions.

routes.label: Data Science program
routes.why: Statistics, SQL, Python and machine learning.

routes.label: Business, then business analytics
routes.why: Learn how companies work, then analyze their numbers.

routes.label: Health Sciences, then health data
routes.why: Combine biology with data to work in hospitals and research labs.

routes.label: Agriculture, then precision agriculture
routes.why: Use data to help farms grow more with less.

destinations.name: Registered Nurse
destinations.blurb: Care for patients and families in hospitals, clinics and communities.

routes.label: Health Sciences toward a nursing degree
routes.why: Biology, anatomy, first aid and care experience.

routes.label: Practical Nursing diploma, then bridge
routes.why: Become a Registered Practical Nurse through college, then bridge to a nursing degree if you want.

steps.title: Compare PN programs
steps.objective: Compare two college Practical Nursing diplomas: admission requirements, length and placements.
steps.learn: Practical nursing programs are a direct route into patient care.

steps.title: Get care experience
steps.objective: Volunteer 20 hours in a hospital, clinic or long-term care home.
steps.learn: Experience confirms nursing is right for you and strengthens applications.

steps.title: Learn about licensing
steps.objective: Read how nurses are registered in your province and what the exam involves.
steps.learn: Nursing is a regulated profession, so licensing is part of every route.

steps.title: Plan your bridge
steps.objective: Find a bridging program from practical nursing to a nursing degree.
steps.learn: Many nurses start as RPNs and bridge to a degree while working.

destinations.name: Mechanical Engineer
destinations.blurb: Design machines, products and systems that move the world.

routes.label: Engineering degree
routes.why: Physics, CAD, electronics and the design process.

routes.label: Engineering technology diploma
routes.why: Become an engineering technologist through college, with options to transfer to a degree later.

steps.title: Compare technology diplomas
steps.objective: Compare two mechanical engineering technology diplomas, including co-op.
steps.learn: Technology programs are hands-on and lead straight to technical jobs.

steps.title: Build a CAD portfolio
steps.objective: Design three parts in free CAD software and export drawings of each.
steps.learn: A portfolio of designs shows practical skill to employers and schools.

steps.title: Learn about certification
steps.objective: Read how engineering technicians and technologists are certified.
steps.learn: Certification shows your skills meet a professional standard.

steps.title: Map a degree transfer
steps.objective: Find which diploma credits would transfer to an engineering degree.
steps.learn: Some students go on to a degree after their diploma.

destinations.name: UX Designer
destinations.blurb: Make apps and websites easy and enjoyable to use.

routes.label: UX & Visual Design program
routes.why: Visual design, user research, prototyping and accessibility.

routes.label: Self-taught portfolio route
routes.why: UX hires often look most closely at your portfolio, so you can build skills while studying anything.

steps.title: Learn the basics free
steps.objective: Read ten articles on usability and user research and note one idea from each.
steps.learn: Strong UX starts with understanding people, not tools.

steps.title: Redesign an app
steps.objective: Pick an app you find annoying and prototype a better version in Figma.
steps.learn: Redesigns are a classic first portfolio piece.

steps.title: Test with real people
steps.objective: Run a usability test with five people and summarize what you changed.
steps.learn: Testing shows you design from evidence.

steps.title: Publish two case studies
steps.objective: Write two portfolio case studies and share them with a designer for feedback.
steps.learn: Case studies are what employers read.

destinations.name: Lawyer
destinations.blurb: Advise and represent people, businesses and governments.

routes.label: Law & Policy, then law school
routes.why: An undergrad in any field, the LSAT, then a law degree.

routes.label: Engineering, then patent law
routes.why: Master engineering design, then cross over to protect inventions.

routes.label: Paralegal route
routes.why: Licensed paralegals in Ontario can represent people in some courts and tribunals after a college program.

steps.title: Learn what paralegals do
steps.objective: Read what licensed paralegals can and can't do in your province.
steps.learn: In Ontario, licensed paralegals can handle some cases on their own.

steps.title: Compare paralegal programs
steps.objective: Compare two accredited college paralegal programs.
steps.learn: An accredited program is required before the licensing exam.

steps.title: Volunteer at a legal clinic
steps.objective: Volunteer or job-shadow at a community legal clinic or law office.
steps.learn: Seeing legal work up close shows you which area you enjoy.

steps.title: Keep law school open
steps.objective: Note what you'd need to apply to law school later, if you choose to.
steps.learn: Some paralegals later become lawyers.

destinations.name: Policy Analyst (Political Science)
destinations.blurb: Research problems and help governments and non-profits decide what to do about them.

routes.label: Law & Policy / Political Science
routes.why: Argument, research, rights and how decisions get made.

routes.label: Data Science, then policy analysis
routes.why: Use data to show what's really happening, then shape policy.

routes.label: Agriculture, then food & environmental policy
routes.why: Bring real farming knowledge to food, land and climate policy.

routes.label: Health Sciences, then health policy
routes.why: Turn health evidence into public rules.

destinations.name: Startup Founder
destinations.blurb: Start and grow a business of your own.

routes.label: Business & Entrepreneurship
routes.why: Money, marketing, pitching and running a venture.

routes.label: Computer Science, then tech entrepreneurship
routes.why: Build the product yourself, then learn to sell it.

routes.label: Build while you study
routes.why: You don't need a business degree to start. Many founders begin with a small project alongside school.

steps.title: Talk to ten customers
steps.objective: Interview ten people who might use your idea and write down their problems.
steps.learn: Founders who listen first build things people actually want.

steps.title: Launch something small
steps.objective: Sell a first version to five people, even if it's simple.
steps.learn: A small launch teaches more than a perfect plan.

steps.title: Find a mentor
steps.objective: Reach out to a local founder or youth entrepreneurship program.
steps.learn: Mentors help you avoid common mistakes.

steps.title: Track your numbers
steps.objective: Track revenue and costs for a month in a spreadsheet.
steps.learn: Knowing your numbers is the core business skill.

destinations.name: Product Manager
destinations.blurb: Decide what a team builds and why.

routes.label: Business & Entrepreneurship
routes.why: Strategy, customers and leading teams.

routes.label: UX Design, then product management
routes.why: User research is a product manager's core skill.

routes.label: Computer Science, then tech entrepreneurship
routes.why: Understand how products are built, then lead them.

destinations.name: Agronomist / Farm Manager
destinations.blurb: Help farms grow healthy crops and run sustainably.

routes.label: Agriculture & Food Systems program
routes.why: Soil and plant science, hands-on farming and agri-tech.

routes.label: College agriculture diploma + farm work
routes.why: A practical diploma plus seasonal farm jobs is a strong, affordable route.

steps.title: Compare ag diplomas
steps.objective: Compare two college agriculture or horticulture diplomas, including placements.
steps.learn: College ag programs are hands-on and closely tied to local farms.

steps.title: Work a growing season
steps.objective: Get a seasonal job or volunteer role on a farm, greenhouse or orchard.
steps.learn: Nothing replaces a season of real farm work.

steps.title: Learn farm data tools
steps.objective: Chart a local crop's yields or weather using a free dataset.
steps.learn: Modern farms run on data as much as tractors.

steps.title: Plan your next step
steps.objective: Decide between working, a degree transfer, or running a farm, and list what each needs.
steps.learn: Diplomas can lead to work or further study.
